cause: after the question was approved and the first five ideas filed

1-build-a-hand-labelled-set-of-drawn-pic.line: Every other idea is measured on this set, so it goes first.

why.impact: Without it no idea can be judged, and it shows how big the gap really is.
why.odds: It is labelling and one run of the existing detector, so it will almost surely produce usable numbers.
why.path: Ideas 2, 3, 4 and 5 all need its labelled pictures.

2-let-the-current-face-detector-see-draw.line: The cheapest possible fix, and it tells size apart from training gap.

why.impact: A win needs no new model, but it may only help large, simply drawn faces.
why.odds: The detector sees faces at about 13 px today, so more size should help some, but a photo-trained detector may still not know drawn faces.
why.path: Its answer says whether a second detector (idea 3) is needed at all.

3-add-a-face-detector-trained-on-anime-a.line: The most likely real fix for drawn faces, but it may lack the face points alignment needs.

why.impact: A detector trained on drawn faces attacks the believed main cause directly.
why.odds: Such detectors exist for anime; Western cartoons and painted styles and the missing five face points are the risks.
why.path: Idea 4 only makes sense once this shows a drawn-face detector works.

5-check-whether-faces-of-the-same-drawn-.line: Tells whether found drawn faces will be useful for clusters and characters at all.

why.impact: If recognition fails on drawn faces, finding them helps thumbnails and crops but not clusters or likeness.
why.odds: ArcFace is trained on real faces, so good separation of drawn characters is unlikely.
why.path: Can use the hand-drawn boxes from idea 1, so it does not wait for a better detector.

4-send-each-picture-to-the-photo-or-the-.line: Only worth doing once idea 3 has shown a drawn-face detector works.

why.impact: It decides how a second detector ships without hurting photos, but adds nothing if idea 3 fails.
why.odds: The WD14 tagger or a CLIP check should tell photos from drawings well, but mixed styles are hard.
